title: What this means for energy traders — Monday, October 12, 2026

sections.overall: Geopolitics and weather dominate the tape. Tanker attacks around the Strait of Hormuz, a Houthi-linked attack on a Saudi airport, a strained Russia-Ukraine "energy ceasefire" and Hurricane Isaias in the US Gulf all feed the same theme: constrained physical supply, with diesel the tightest link. Against that, company-led trends in LNG are cooling this week, while biochar carbon removal is the one ledger trend gaining momentum.
sections.CRUDE_OIL: CNBC reports Brent above $106 after the Saudi airport attack, and the FT says prices rose as the ceasefire frayed. Markets typically price in shipping-lane risk and policy shifts quickly, and headline reversals in either direction are common. The DOE's SPR exchange authorization addresses hurricane-related disruption rather than the Middle East. What remains unclear is how long Gulf of Mexico output is affected and whether Hormuz transit recovers.
sections.NATURAL_GAS: Hurricane Isaias disrupted US oil and gas production and left households without power, per the FT. On the commercial side, LNG deal-making with Asian buyers and US export expansion both show FADING trajectories in the ledger, though ADNOC's Gulf Group agreement is dated today. Weekly US LNG shipments dropped to 31. A slower announcement cadence is not the same as slower physical flows; the two should not be conflated.
sections.REFINED_PRODUCTS: Diesel is the central story. The US-Russia diesel arrangement drew criticism, and analysts quoted by The Guardian and CNBC see limited near-term effect because volumes are small and shipping takes weeks. Damaged refineries in the Middle East and Russia keep margins elevated, and the FT frames the crisis as a test for global trade. Whether the deal is carried out in full is unclear.
sections.CARBON_CREDITS: Methodology and policy news was heavy: Verra's first rice credits, clean cooking access to the UN market, and IMO guidance on marine removal. UK carbon prices reached their highest since January with the EU-UK ETS link on next month's summit agenda. Corporate removal purchases are FADING this week, while biochar supply expansion is RISING.
